sources.entry: PowerShell - PowerShell is a cross-platform automation and configuration tool/framework that works well with your existing tools.

summary.one_liner: PowerShell is a cross-platform automation, configuration, and scripting shell and framework for Windows, Linux, and macOS, with a command-line shell, scripting language, and cmdlet processing framework.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes PowerShell as a cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS) automation and configuration tool and framework. It is optimized for working with structured data such as JSON, CSV, and XML, REST APIs, and object models. It includes a command-line shell, an associated scripting language, and a framework for processing cmdlets. The repository started as a fork of Windows PowerShell, but changes here are not ported back to Windows PowerShell 5.1, and issues tracked here cover PowerShell 7.x and higher. The README links to build instructions for Linux, Windows, and macOS, a contribution guide, a developer FAQ, and a PowerShell SDK NuGet package for .NET developers. Many of the links in the README are empty in this copy, so some destinations are unknown.
use_cases: process JSON, CSV, or XML data from the command line
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL shown as empty in the README>
See docs/building/linux.md, docs/building/windows-core.md, or docs/building/macos.md for build instructions
notable: Cross-platform support for Windows, Linux, and macOS
Built-in handling of structured data such as JSON, CSV, and XML
Fork of Windows PowerShell; issues here apply to PowerShell 7.x and higher
Published PowerShell SDK NuGet package for .NET C# applications
Community chat on Discord, IRC, and Slack
caveats: Changes are not ported back to Windows PowerShell 5.1
The README states the PowerShell container images at mcr.microsoft.com/powershell are no longer maintained; the .NET team now maintains them
